data.title: YZi Labs Head to Join UN Digital Cooperation Day 2026 Panel on Tokenization and Public Infrastructure
data.description:
YZi Labs Managing Partner and Head Ella Zhang will join the panel “Blockchain and the Tokenized Future: Sovereign Choices and Safeguards for Next-Gen DPI” at UN Digital Cooperation Day 2026. YZi Labs posted on X.

The discussion will examine tokenization beyond digital currencies, including land, securities, and commodities, as well as how prepared countries are and what safeguards are needed before tokenized rails can be integrated into public infrastructure.

The panel is scheduled for Monday, 21 September, from 13:30–14:30 ET in New York. YZi Labs thanked @ODET_UN and @PakistanVARA for the invitation.

data.title: Linera Founder Says Project Will Stop Operations After Fundraising Falls Short
data.description:
Linera founder Mathieu Baudet announced on Discord that the project will stop operations immediately after its fundraising efforts fell short. According to PANews, Baudet said token sales on Sonar drew about $900,000 in subscription commitments, but the amount did not reach the minimum required to complete the sale, and all subscription funds have been returned to participants.

Baudet also said the team tried to raise emergency funding to keep operations running until mainnet launch, but it was unable to secure the needed capital. He said this ultimately led to the project’s closure. Earlier reports said Linera’s LNRA community round received 848,300 USDC in commitments, below the 1.5 million USDC minimum target, and would be refunded.

data.title: Radix Foundation Reports Exploit of Unseen Radix Engine Vulnerability
data.description:
Radix Foundation said an attacker used an undiscovered vulnerability in Radix Engine to withdraw assets from third-party vaults without owner authorization, then bridged them through Hyperlane to networks including Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Solana before selling them. According to Odaily, the flaw originated from a code cleanup in June 2023, and an independent security audit by Zellic in August 2024 did not detect it.

About three hours after the incident, Radix validators took enough stake offline to prevent the network from reaching consensus and stop further exploitation. The affected assets included ETH, WBTC, USDT, USDC, BNB, and SOL. Radix said the fix has been completed and independently reviewed and tested, and network recovery is now underway.

data.title: SEC Receives Amended S-1/A for 21Shares Injective ETF as Altcoin ETF Race Heats Up
data.description:
The SEC has received an amended registration statement for the 21Shares Injective ETF, moving the proposed fund a step closer to becoming a publicly traded product, according to Crypto Briefing. The amended S-1/A updates the original October 2025 filing and would give traditional investors regulated access to INJ, the native token of the Injective Network. If approved, the ETF would list on Nasdaq under the ticker TINJ, passively tracking INJ via the FTSE Injective Index, with a twist: discretionary staking of a portion of holdings to boost returns.

Structured as a Delaware statutory trust and sponsored by 21Shares US LLC, the fund's original S-1 landed on October 20, 2025, and the latest amendment keeps the registration active as the review continues. The preliminary prospectus notes shares have not traded publicly and no financial statements are included yet. INJ staking rewards ranged from 9.3% to 13.62% annually in 2025, giving the ETF a yield dimension most equity-focused products cannot match. As of September 1, 2026, INJ's circulating supply stood at about 92.8 million tokens, with a market capitalization near $488 million.

21Shares is no stranger to wrapping digital assets in traditional packaging, already offering a 21Shares Injective Staking ETP to European investors and having been among the first issuers of spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs via its ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF partnership. Since spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024 and Ethereum products followed later that year, asset managers have raced to file for funds covering Solana, XRP, Litecoin, Cardano and a growing list of layer-1 and DeFi tokens.

Injective is a layer-1 blockchain built on the Cosmos SDK for decentralized finance, focused on decentralized exchanges, derivatives and cross-chain trading. Its low-double-digit staking yield offers a tailwind pure price-tracking products can't replicate. The $488 million market cap is notable: for comparison, Bitcoin's is in the trillions and Ethereum's typically above $200 billion, so an INJ ETF drawing even tens of millions could represent a meaningful share of the token's float. The choice of the FTSE Injective Index — from London Stock Exchange Group's FTSE Russell — is also notable as the firm expands its digital-asset indexes, while custody arrangements remain unfinalized, a detail the SEC will likely want settled before any approval.

data.title: Trump Says Son Will Repay Wedding Party Costs Funded by Russian Oligarch
data.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said his son, Donald Trump Jr., told him he would repay a Russian oligarch who funded his May wedding celebration in the Bahamas. According to Sina Finance, Democratic lawmakers in Congress launched an investigation this week after reports said Russian businessman and International Boxing Association President Umar Kremlev paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for the event. Trump told reporters on Friday that when he asked his son about the reports, Donald Trump Jr. replied, "Dad, I will pay the money back." A person familiar with the matter confirmed that Donald Trump Jr. plans to reimburse Kremlev.

data.title: US MARKET CLOSE | Chip Stocks Rebound as Philadelphia Semiconductor Index Rises Over 2%; Oil Falls Below $100
data.description: US stocks closed mixed on Friday as investors continued to digest the Federal Reserve's first rate hike in three years and concerns tied to artificial intelligence, according to Sina Finance. The Dow fell 95.39 points, or 0.18%, to 51,682.64, ending the week down 1.69%. The S&P 500 rose 12.74 points, or 0.17%, to 7,650.50, down 0.08% for the week. The Nasdaq gained 104.24 points, or 0.39%, to 26,522.54, up 0.72% for the week. The "Magnificent Seven" were mixed: Nvidia and Amazon rose more than 1%, Google edged higher, Meta fell more than 2%, while Apple, Microsoft and Tesla dipped slightly. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index surged late in the session to close up 2.78%. SanDisk jumped about 11%, Coherent rose more than 7%, Seagate Technology gained more than 6%, Western Digital advanced more than 4%, Micron Technology rose more than 3%, and AMD and SK Hynix each climbed more than 2%. Cryptocurrency-related names rallied, with Strategy up more than 16%, MARA Holdings up more than 13%, Robinhood up more than 9%, Bitmine and Cipher up more than 8%, and Circle up more than 7%. Rising Treasury yields pressured equities. The 10-year Treasury yield broke above 5% earlier in the week, touching its highest level since July 2007, and briefly returned above that mark on Friday after pulling back Thursday, last up nearly 6 basis points at 5.006%. US crude closed roughly flat for the week but held above $100 a barrel. On Friday, West Texas Intermediate futures fell 1.58% to settle at $100.30 a barrel, while global benchmark Brent futures fell 0.91% to settle at $103.87 a barrel. The Fed on Wednesday decided to raise rates by 25 basis points and signaled at least one more hike this year, driving major averages lower that day, though the market rebounded Thursday. The Thursday rebound, especially in tech, suggested investors were eager to look past the prospect of higher-for-longer rates and return to the AI narrative, betting it will continue to support corporate profits. "Some of the uncertainty was removed after the Fed hike this week," said Scott Welch, chief investment officer at Certuity. But Welch does not view the latest hike as a one-off, believing the hiking cycle is just beginning and could weigh on stocks in the coming months. "At some point, whether in October or after the election, I think the Fed will raise rates at least once more in 2026, and possibly once or twice more in 2027," he said. He forecasts continued upward pressure on Treasury yields and expects oil prices to stay elevated in the coming months. Chip stocks have largely recovered from the sell-off earlier in the week that followed calls from Anthropic and OpenAI to slow AI development. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index posted a small gain for the week.

data.title: Shielded Labs CEO Says Zcash Uses Rough Consensus Governance Model
data.description:
Shielded Labs CEO Jason McGee said Zcash uses a rough consensus governance model based on multiple stakeholders. Holder votes and community committee votes are used to gauge sentiment and inform decisions, but they are not binding.

According to Odaily, protocol changes usually require broad support from the community committee and token holders, while the final decision rests with stakeholders that operate and use the network, including node operators, miners, exchanges, wallets, and users.

McGee said no single group can push through protocol changes on its own. He added that the model can coordinate network upgrades when needed while preventing any one group from unilaterally driving changes.

data.title: India’s Growth Faces Infrastructure Strains as Bangalore Tech Boom Draws Capital
data.description:
India’s technology sector has powered growth in the world’s fastest-growing large economy, but uneven progress has left some strengths vulnerable, according to Bloomberg.

Bangalore became India’s tech capital by attracting global investment and building a deep talent pool, but infrastructure and policies have struggled to keep pace with the expansion. The program also looks at whether Hyderabad can overtake Bangalore as India’s leading tech city and Blackstone’s investment in Royal Challengers Bengaluru.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Jensen Huang Urges Faster AI Development
data.description:
Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang said technology companies should keep pushing ahead with artificial intelligence research, even as some industry leaders have warned that development may need to slow. According to Sina Finance, Huang said companies should accelerate as much as possible and should not release products before they are ready or introduce unsafe products.

Huang said Nvidia would move at full speed, but it would not and should not release products before they are mature. He added that no one expects the company to do that, and that everyone expects it to succeed and help the United States achieve greater prosperity.

The comments come as concerns about the pace of AI development have intensified in recent weeks, with some people calling for guardrails and government regulation. The debate was partly sparked by Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who resigned earlier this month and said AI companies were rushing innovation at the expense of complete safety standards.

Coxon said AI could pose a threat to humanity if left unchecked. U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration has so far generally not agreed with those concerns.

Days later, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei appeared to share some of Coxon’s concerns. He said the industry had long misled the public about the risks of the technology and described its development as exponential, while adding that there was no need to panic or shut down all related research. Amodei said the situation was a warning sign and that the pace needed to slow.

data.title: Morgan Stanley Limits Redemptions Again at Nearly $7 Billion Private Credit Fund
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Morgan Stanley again capped redemptions at its nearly $7 billion private credit fund in the third quarter, with redemption requests more than twice the amount the fund was willing to buy back. North Haven Private Income Fund set its redemption cap at 5%, while investors requested redemptions for 11.4% of shares, roughly unchanged from the previous three months. In the three quarters through September, the fund completed about $479 million in buybacks, and nearly two-thirds of the requests came from investors restricted in the previous two rounds.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Rejects AI Doomsday Claims, Says 2030 World-End Probability Is 0%
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang again rejected AI doomsday claims, saying the technology will not pose an existential threat to humanity and that the probability of a world-ending scenario in 2030 is 0%.
